reasoning: The two attempts are nearly equivalent: they have the same model.json, correct script placement, handling for players who joined early, and SetCore retries. B wins narrowly. It always shows its one-time notification, including a message when the kit is empty, while A sends nothing when every count is 0. B also avoids overwriting counts that are already set, and it uses the conventional instance-path require. A's exact-path lookup and its stricter checks on attribute values partly offset this, but not fully.

criteria.criterion: StarterKit declared in mapped Rojo files
criteria.note: src/ReplicatedStorage/Shared/StarterKit.model.json has className Configuration and attributes, which builds ReplicatedStorage.Shared.StarterKit.
Brick 20, Dirt 20, Grass 10, Window 0 and Wood 10 are all JSON numbers.
StarterKit.server.luau is under ServerScriptService and StarterKit.client.luau is under StarterPlayerScripts.

criteria.criterion: Reads StarterKit at real path, covers all BlockTypes
criteria.note: The server reads ReplicatedStorage.Shared.StarterKit, loops over BlockTypes.List, and getStarterCount warns and returns 0 for a missing, NaN, negative or infinite value.

criteria.criterion: Existing players, one-time notification, SetCore guard
criteria.note: It loops over Players:GetPlayers(), waits for all counts using AttributeChanged with a disconnect, and wraps SetCore in pcall with 20 retries, but sends no notification when every count is 0.
There are only three new files, and luau-lsp, selene, StyLua and rojo build all pass.

criteria.criterion: StarterKit declared in mapped Rojo files
criteria.note: Its StarterKit.model.json is identical to A's, at src/ReplicatedStorage/Shared.
StarterKit.server.luau is under ServerScriptService and StarterKitNotification.client.luau is under StarterPlayerScripts.

criteria.criterion: Reads StarterKit at real path, covers all BlockTypes
criteria.note: It finds the kit with FindFirstChild(CONFIG_NAME, true) and checks IsA, which works but is looser than indexing the exact path, and it warns and gives 0 when an attribute is missing or invalid for any type in BlockTypes.List.

criteria.criterion: Existing players, one-time notification, SetCore guard
criteria.note: It uses task.spawn over GetPlayers(), waitForCounts loops on AttributeChanged:Wait(), the notification runs once at the end of the script with a fallback message for zero counts, and SetCore sits in pcall with 20 retries.
There are only three new files, and all checks pass.

strengths: Indexes the exact path the files produce
Thorough validation of attribute values, including NaN and infinity
The one-time AttributeChanged connection is disconnected after it fires
weaknesses: Sends no notification at all when every count is 0
Overwrites counts that may already be set on the player
Depends on newer syntax (const and the @game require alias)

strengths: Always shows the notification, including a message when the kit is empty
Doesn't overwrite counts that are already set
Standard instance-path require with clear header comments
Separate warnings for a missing attribute and a wrong type
weaknesses: A recursive FindFirstChild could pick up a different instance named StarterKit
Doesn't treat infinite values as invalid
